title: Emergency Pathway: compact UX lattice for rapid rollback and surge mitigation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Multiple incidents showed operators needed a condensed, clearly signposted path inside the Redwood Console to execute emergency rollbacks and mitigate sudden traffic surges. Current rollout surfaces are verbose and rely on deep navigation — during incidents teams want < 3 clicks to enact a safe fallback and get diagnostic signals.

Goal: Design a compact ‘Emergency Pathway’ UX lattice (a minimal, scannable modal + micro-dashboard) that 1) surfaces immediate controls for rollback/traffic snapback, dark launch quarantine, and tranche isolation; 2) shows key telemetry signals and quick heuristics (error rate delta, latency P95, model quality drift) with built-in guardrails; 3) provides clear audit and revert plan text for SRE/PM handoff; 4) works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers with consistent affordances.

Out of scope: full traffic simulation canvas, long-form canary composition flows, deep experiment authoring. This is explicitly a compact emergency surface to complement existing rollout composer flows.
acceptance_criteria: Compact modal opens from any rollout detail with a single keyboard shortcut and a pinned header action
Primary emergency actions: Immediate rollback (instant), Quarantine variant (isolate), Traffic-shift to fallback model (50/50 -> 0/100) are present with clear confirm steps
Telemetry strip in modal displays three prioritized signals with thresholds and live sparkline: error-rate, P95 latency, quality-regression-score
Action confirmation shows predicted downstream impact (approx. latency/cost delta) and writes a draft audit log message editable before submit
Design has accessible colours, clear affordances for mobile/responsive console widths, and matches console design tokens
Design artifacts include annotated Figma frames, a clickable prototype, and copy for microcopy + error states
design_notes: Introduce a bounded modal (max-width 720px) with a three-column lattice: left = actions, center = telemetry quickstrip, right = quick-reason & draft audit message
Action affordances: primary destructive action highlighted in red with two-step confirm; 'Quarantine' is reversible and uses a soft-warning style
Telemetry heuristics: default thresholds (can be tuned per-customer) and inline explainers for why signal is high; show last 10m delta and a 1h baseline
Fallback target selection: prioritize same-arch compatible variants; if none, show 'route to safe-hosted-variant' option with cost delta estimate
Include a compact 'rehearse' toggle that runs a dry-run (no traffic change) and reports simulation results in the modal — only available to users with toggle permission
Edge cases: network partition between Console and Private control-plane must show offline fallback info and the modal should surface CLI commands that SRE can run locally
Performance: modal must load telemetry in <300ms for hosted accounts; lazy-load extended graphs after initial render
Accessibility: keyboard-first flow, confirmation dialogs trap focus; descriptive ARIA labels for each action and signal value
